page: Amazon Web Services r7i.48xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and x86_64 architecture. It features 192 virtual CPUs mapped to 96 physical Intel Xeon 8488C cores running at 3.2 GHz, with two threads per core. The processor includes a 105 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions and Advanced Vector Extensions. The instance is equipped with 1536.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. It does not include local storage or GPUs, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core CPU performance, with the stress-ng multi-core test and PassMark CPU score placing in the top 10% of tested servers. Memory bandwidth is also in the top 10% for both cached small-block reads and uncached large-block read/write operations. In database-specific workloads, the instance achieves top-tier results, executing 183.87 million Redis SET operations per second and scoring in the top 10% for PassMark database operations. Single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core and PassMark memory scores falling in the middle 50% average tier.

This instance is designed for memory-intensive workloads that require substantial parallel processing capabilities. It is suited for large-scale in-memory databases, key-value stores like Redis, and complex database operations. The inclusion of Intel AMX instructions enables strong performance in CPU-based machine learning tasks, as demonstrated by strong top 25% scores in large-model LLM inference prompt processing and text generation. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high density of DDR5 memory combined with 192 dedicated vCPUs provides a consolidated platform for resource-heavy enterprise applications, though the lack of local NVMe storage requires external network-attached storage solutions.
